jobs.title: CoverMyMeds Product Marketing Intern- Summer 2027 at McKesson
jobs.description: Employer: McKesson Expires: 11/13/2026 About the RoleThis summer, you'll join a B2B healthcare product marketing team and help accelerate its impact — using AI to move from one-off prompts to autonomous, workflow-level agents that change how the team operates. CoverMyMeds is seeking a curious, analytical intern interested in the craft of product marketing (positioning, messaging, buyer insight, enablement, go-to-market) and sees AI as a force multiplier for that craft, not a substitute for it. The ideal candidate is a marketer at heart: passionate about understanding buyers, shaping how products are positioned and brought to market, and telling stories that resonate — and excited to apply AI to do all of it faster, sharper, and at greater scale. What You'll DoDoing the PMM work, faster — you'll help drive smarter product marketing workstreams — product positioning and messaging, buyer and competitive insights, commercial enablement, go-to-market support — and use AI to move through them.Moving from assistants to agents — help us graduate from one-off AI prompts to repeatable, semi-autonomous workflows that run parts of our process.Driving participation — be a champion for AI adoption across the team: demo tools, run enablement sessions, lower the barrier to entry for teammates who are AI-curious but not yet AI-confident.Measuring success — help define what "AI-enabled product marketing impact" means, then build the tracking.Optimizing impact with AI — find the highest-leverage places where AI can speed up actionable market signals, sharpen messaging, or scale our output, and prove it with results.Where you might plug in (you won't do all of these — you'll go deep where the business needs you most):Positioning & messagingPersonas & segmentationSales enablementGo-to-market planning What You'll GainHands-on experience in B2B healthcare technology and product marketing, with a dedicated mentor.Exposure to how a Fortune-class healthcare business runs product marketing.Ownership of 1-2 projects, giving experience applying AI and automation to real business challenges.Opportunities to influence how a modern marketing organization evolves from traditional workflows to AI-powered ways of working. QualificationsA marketing student — pursuing Marketing, Business, Communications, or related degree— with a genuine interest in product marketing craft (positioning, messaging, buyer insight) and a curiosity for AI amplification.Strong interest in AI, marketing technology, and innovation.Excellent research, analytical, and communication skills.Experience with generative AI tools such as Copilot, Writer, ChatGPT, Claude, or similar.Comfort with ambiguity, a bias towards action and curiosity about healthcare Success in This RoleBy the end of the internship, you will have helped increase Product Marketing output, accelerated research and content development, improved AI adoption across key workflows, and contributed to measurable gains in team efficiency and strategic impact. Join us in helping redefine the future of Product Marketing through AI.

jobs.description: Employer: J. Paul Getty Trust Expires: 11/14/2026 The Getty Post-Baccalaureate Conservation Internships aim to increase the number of students from underrepresented backgrounds preparing to enroll in graduate degree programs related to museum conservation. An advanced degree is essential to a conservation career and few programs exist. Applicants often boost their credentials by completing prerequisite courses and undertaking up to thousands of hours of conservation training, usually unpaid. Graduate program administrators say these realities have limited opportunities for underrepresented groups.Launched in 2020 as a pilot program, the Getty Post-Baccalaureate Internships are the first nationwide effort to provide yearlong financial support and hands-on conservation experience to underrepresented post-baccalaureates who are preparing to apply to conservation graduate programs. EligibilityWhile these internships are intended for students from backgrounds underrepresented in the conservation field, Getty encourages eligible candidates from all backgrounds to apply for consideration. Getty is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of any protected trait under the law. Candidates will have the opportunity to demonstrate their interest in museum conservation and how they might add new and underrepresented perspectives, which can include – among other things – socio-economic status, cultural background, physical or other disability, geographical origin, and/or any other life experiences.Candidates must:-Be a United States citizen or permanent resident eligible to work in the United States (permanent residents are non-citizens authorized to live and work in the United States on a permanent basis, also known as "green card" holders). Those with DACA (Deferred Action for Childhood Arrival) status valid through the internship period are also eligible.-Be committed to a career in conservation and possess a strong desire to attend graduate school to further that goal.-Be able to demonstrate previous experience in conservation. Terms of the GrantAll positions are full-time for 12 months from September 7, 2027 — August 25, 2028. Interns are placed at conservation studios and labs at the Getty Center or Getty Villa for their first six months, and then at a local Los Angeles museum or within a different Getty department for the second six months.Grant AmountThe grant amount is $45,500 for 12 months plus $1,500 towards relocation expenses to Los Angeles. The internship includes an additional $4,000 towards educational reimbursements, certificate courses in conservation, domestic conservation conference attendance, or other professional-development opportunities related to the internship. Housing is not provided. Interns are eligible to enroll in Getty's healthcare plan at a subsidized cost. Please note that grant funds may be subject to federal and state taxes and deductions.Prerequisite Course for Graduate SchoolDuring spring 2028, interns may enroll in a prerequisite course (chemistry, art history, studio art, and/or foreign language) at a local community college to help fulfill the requirements for their graduate school applications. In addition to support from their supervisors, interns will also have the support of an academic advisor Collaborating InstitutionsInternships are offered at the conservation studios and labs at the Getty Center in Los Angeles and the Getty Villa in Malibu, along with local Los Angeles museums. For the 2027-2028 internship year, placements are being offered at the following Getty departments and institutions:Getty Conservation Institute Collections Department and Los Angeles County Museum of ArtGetty Conservation Institute Science Department and The HuntingtonGetty Research Institute Conservation and Preservation Department and the Autry Museum of the American WestJ. Paul Getty Museum Antiquities Conservation Department and the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences Margaret Herrick Library

(Median salary is $675/week)Applicants can choose which internship programs they would like to be considered for:+ Audience Engagement: These internships vary by newsroom, but the mission always remains the same—to help the news find its audience. From writing SEO-friendly headlines and producing engaging content for video and social to crafting newsletters and seizing on trending topics on social media, job expectations vary. Previous internship placements include: Palm Beach Post, The Marshall Project, Oakland Voices and Houston Chronicle.+ Business Reporting: We place reporters in more than 30 newsrooms across the country covering a wide variety of topics from Wall Street to Main Street, including markets, economic trends, new businesses, emerging entrepreneurs, labor unions, real estate, climate change, agriculture and automotive industries. Previous internship placements include: The Wall Street Journal, American City Business Journals, Barron’s, Insider, Fortune, American Banker, Detroit News and Automotive News.+ Data Journalism: There are three different types of data internships we usually place interns in: 1) heavy emphasis on filing records requests and analyzing data using spreadsheets; 2) reporting and writing using government data or assisting investigative reporting projects; and 3) using coding and technical tools to build apps and interactive visuals for news stories. Previous internship placements include: Arkansas Democrat-Gazette, Detroit News, Maryland Matters and Investigative Reporting Workshop.+ Digital Media: Working as a digital media intern means many different things, depending on the newsroom. You could be working in print, social, video, audio or all of it. Interns receive across-the-board training so they can expand their skill sets using the latest technology and storytelling techniques. Previous internship placements include: Hawaii Public Radio, Kansas City Public Television, Oakland Voices and Storyful.+ Multiplatform Editing: Editors are the final check on a story before it is published. Multiplatform editing interns assess copy for accuracy, completeness, tone and style while also writing SEO-friendly headlines and designing pages on deadline. Previous internship placements include: The New York Times, Los Angeles Times, The Washington Post, Stars & Stripes and San Francisco Chronicle.The pre-internship training dates typically fall between May 17-June 12. Internships traditionally start the first or second week of June.

You'll join a cohort of around 50 other dynamic interns for a 12-week program packed with hands on learning. Throughout the summer you will dive into real projects that will give you a taste of what it's like to work in a leading business and manufacturing environment. Sharpen your skills with interactive workshops on networking, public speaking, and using AI tools in a business environment. Connect with mentors and see all areas of the office and manufacturing processes. By the end of the summer, you'll leave with real skills, an expanded professional network, and memories to last a lifetime. This is your chance to take your career to new heights! jobs.description: Employer: WETA Expires: 11/20/2026 Start Date: 12/4/2026End Date: 4/2/2027Preferred Year in School:Rising SeniorRising JuniorGraduate StudentPOSITION OVERVIEWGet a deep dive into Communications work as the WETA Communications intern for Spring 2026. Writing and proofreading skills are very important, along with excellent organizational skills and real enthusiasm for teamwork on events.The intern will support the WETA Communications team as it develops and execute communications and events that effectively engage audiences in the D.C. area and across the national public media system. Links to short-form writing or project samples are encouraged.PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIESSupport a busy and dedicated Communications team across corporate communications projects, events, and media outreach, including:Develop editorial skill by contributing to corporate communications projects, including photo research and editing/proofreadingAssist with a building-wide environmental design and storytelling brand projectBuild and track audiences for public events to include outreach to organizations and registration/RSVPsWork with a team on advance and day-of support for event logisticsWrite and edit blurbs/articles about tv, online and classical music programs for use in media pitching, promotions, and publicationsConduct media research, build media lists, and report on media coverage using Muck Rack databaseOrganize and categorize photo and publicity assets using digital asset management systemEDUCATIONPreferred Major: Demonstrated interest in media, history, arts, theater, humanities, communications and/or public affairsLEARNING OBJECTIVESUnderstand the public media system and the many opportunities for careers in the fieldGain broad knowledge and direct experience in a range of corporate communications and media relations roles in working for a major content producer at a leading non-profitApply learned writing, editing and proofreading skills to real-life publications and situations, with your own specific projects to showcase your skillsDESIRED COMPETENCIESProactive organizationArchival/research skillsWriting and proofreadingCollaborative and flexible teamworkAttention to detailPlus, bring your special extra skills, i.e. photography, graphic design, languages, talent management, public events, etc.ADDITIONAL SKILLS AND QUALIFICATIONSHelpful to have fluency in Excel, Claude, Word, PowerPoint, and other softwareLOCATIONWETA and NewsHour Productions are Washington, DC established media and news organizations. WETA is also home to PBS News, the primary daily, breaking, and special news producer for PBS. jobs.title: MBA Marketing Intern at Graco Inc.
jobs.description: Employer: Graco Inc. Expires: 11/21/2026 The purpose of this position is to provide immersive, strategic-level experience within Graco’s Category Marketing team. At Graco, Category Marketing focuses on understanding and growing specific customer segments and industries (often referred to as market verticals), helping the business identify opportunities, understand customer needs, and shape strategies that drive growth. In this role, the intern will lead a defined strategic project for an assigned customer segment under the mentorship of the Director of Category Marketing. The intern will leverage market research, Voice of Customer (VOC) insights, competitive analysis, and go-to-market strategy to address a real business challenge. The experience culminates in the development and presentation of a strategic recommendation to Graco’s Executive Leadership Team. This internship is designed for MBA candidates seeking a long-term career in category marketing, product marketing, strategic marketing, or general management. Program Structure: This summer internship is centered on a high-value strategic project that addresses a real business opportunity or challenge within an assigned category and which has the potential to shape future growth initiatives. The project is supplemented by exposure to the broader category marketing function and close collaboration with cross-functional partners, including product management, channel marketing, corporate marketing, and sales. The internship culminates in a strategic recommendation presented to senior internship. What You Will Do at Graco Strategic Project Experience Lead a high-impact strategic project focused on a real business opportunity or challenge within an assigned customer segment or industry. Work closely with a Category Marketing leader to define the project scope, conduct analysis, and develop recommendations. Apply market research, customer insights, and business strategy concepts to address a meaningful business question. Develop and present a final recommendation to senior leaders at the conclusion of the internship. Market and Customer Insights Conduct market, customer, and competitive research to better understand industry trends and customer needs. Analyze Voice of Customer (VOC) feedback and other data sources to identify key insights and opportunities. Learn how customer and market insights are used to shape busness and marketing strategies. Cross-Functional Collaboration Collaborate with teams across product management, sales, channel marketing, and corporate marketing Gain exposure to how strategy is developed and translated into product launches, marketing campaigns, and commercial execution. Coordinate with internal subject matter experts to validate research findings and assumptions. Participate in team meetings, project reviews, and business discussions to better understand Graco's growth strategy. Professional Development Build skills in strategic thinking, business analysis, executive communication, and problem solving. Receive coaching and mentorship from experienced marketing leaders throughout the internship. Develop and deliver a professional executive-level presentation summarizing project findings and recommendations. Other duties and learning opportunities as assigned. What You Will Bring to Graco Currently pursuing an MBA, with an expected graduation date within 12–18 months of the internship Bachelor's degree in Marketing, Business Administration, or a related field Prior experience in marketing, business strategy, or vertical-specific market development (internship or professional) preferred Team collaborator with experience working in multi-functional or global team settings Strong analytical skills with the ability to interpret and synthesize VOC insights and market research into clear recommendations Excellent communication and presentation skills, including comfort presenting to senior leadership Ability to manage ambiguity and drive a project forward with limited day-to-day direction

jobs.description: Employer: Altitude Promotions Expires: 11/26/2026 The Sales & Marketing Internship at Altitude Promotions offers a fast-paced, hands-on introduction to the world of B2B sales and marketing. Interns gain real-world experience representing Fortune 500 clients, managing professional relationships with business owners, and learning how to drive revenue growth through strategic marketing and sales initiatives. As part of being an intern at Altitude Promotions, interns will work closely with various teams across the company — including Sales, Public Relations, and Human Resources — to gain a full understanding of how different departments operate together to achieve company goals. Interns start by learning the fundamentals of sales: building client relationships, communicating value, and developing confidence through direct interaction with businesses. jobs.description: Employer: Camp Carl Expires: 11/30/2026 We are looking for applicants ages 16-24 who are Christ-Centered, Relationally Focused, and Incredibly Fun! All of our staff come ready for a life-changing summer where they are challenged in new ways, growing spiritually, and investing in campers for the sake of the Gospel.This position will help tell the story of summer camp at Camp Carl through photography and videography. We are a Christian Summer Camp in Ravenna, Ohio. The media team will gain experience with professional-grade cameras and will be required to carry out several media responsibilities using our provided equipment, software, and spaces. There are daily editing tasks and deadlines along with weekly video editing opportunities. Each team member will spend the day taking photos and filming for our weekly recap video. There is endless creative opportunity, as well as social media content creation experience. We use the Adobe Creative Cloud programs, primarily Adobe Premiere and Adobe Lightroom, to carry out our day-to-day tasks. Team members will live on camp property and be fed (really yummy camp food) while working. A week of camp runs from Sunday afternoon through Friday evening. We ask that applicants commit to most of the summer. In addition, to help you be well-equipped for the role and enfolded into an amazing summer staff team, staff orientation and training days are required before summer begins. It's fun, intentional, and helpful! This experience is unlike any other. You will spend the entire summer gaining media experience while having FUN and sharing Christ with kids!College Credit & Internships - It is possible to work at camp AND receive college credit. Employees must also agree to the standards outlined in our employee handbook regarding morality and lifestyle so that we are aligned in beliefs and values.

jobs.title: Summer 2027 Social Media Internship at Huntington Bank
jobs.description: Employer: Huntington Bank Expires: 11/30/2026 Summary: Huntington’s internship programs provide emerging talent with meaningful, hands‑on experience aligned to their area of study. Over the course of the interns’ time at Huntington, they gain exposure to key business functions across all segments of the organization. An intern’s experience should be focused on professional growth, skill development, and practical application of academic learning. Interns participate in a structured series of development opportunities, including interactions with senior leadership and career pathing insights. The experience also includes immersion in Huntington’s award‑winning culture through community involvement and team‑based activities. Internships at Huntington are designed to help students build a strong foundation for future career success while contributing to meaningful business initiatives. Internship Opportunities at Huntington: Huntington offers internship opportunities for students who are currently enrolled in an academic program and seeking practical, hands‑on experience in their field of study. Internships take place during a defined period of time and are available across all business segments. Rising juniors (Winter 2028 or Spring 2029 grads) may participate in Huntington's Foundations Program, an 8-week, regionally focused experience where students partner directly with a manager and team, contribute to meaningful projects, build professional skills, and explore career opportunities across Huntington and the financial services industry. All interns participate in a variety of developmental and professional activities designed to support learning and exposure to the organization. Depending on your school year, program components may include: Experience in day‑to‑day responsibilities related to their assigned team Exposure to broader business functions A structured schedule of professional development sessions Opportunities to engage with members of the Executive Leadership Team Discussions with senior leaders regarding career paths and Huntington’s business areas A team project focused on applying Huntington’s innovation framework to a business‑relevant problem Participation in volunteer activities and internal events aligned with Huntington’s culture Social Media Internship Overview Huntington Bank is seeking creative, curious and collaborative college students to join our Social Media Internship Program.Eligibility note: This internship is open to rising college juniors enrolled during Summer 2027 at one of the Huntington partner schools for this program: University of Michigan, University of Minnesota, West Virginia University, University of Texas, The Ohio State University, University of Mississippi, University of Alabama or Mississippi State University.This internship offers hands-on experience across the full social media content lifecycle within a highly regulated industry. Interns will join Huntington’s editorial content team and work alongside social media, brand, creative, video and production partners to learn how content moves from initial concept through creation, approval, publication and performance evaluation.Each intern will come from one of Huntington’s partner universities and bring their campus perspective into the program. Working remotely from their home communities, with hybrid in-office participation for Columbus-based interns, interns will contribute ideas, insights and content recommendations that help Huntington connect with customers, communities and university audiences across our footprint. As part of the experience, each intern will develop localized content guidance that reflects their campus, student audience and community context. Duties & Responsibilities: Collaborate with fellow interns and mentors to develop social media concepts grounded in audience needs, business goals, cultural moments and emerging platform opportunities.Participate in brainstorming, creative reviews and content planning discussions by presenting concepts, explaining recommendations and contributing constructive feedback.Work with the editorial content team member who creates and delivers Huntington’s advice and guidance newsletter to identify relevant articles and incorporate them into social plans in ways that are useful, timely and audience-aware.Create, edit, optimize and adapt content for a variety of social platforms and formats, including original photo or video content when opportunities arise and repurposed brand, event or partnership assets.Develop a localized social content toolkit, guide or plan for their Huntington partner university, helping the team understand campus culture, student needs, relevant moments and content opportunities, then present their recommendations to the brand team and other relevant Huntington stakeholders at the end of the internship.Support content planning, workflow management, project execution and performance analysis to help improve future social media content. What You'll LearnContent Strategy, Concept Development & Audience Insight: Learn how leading brands identify audience needs, generate ideas and build content strategies that support business objectives, audience engagement, relevant cultural moments and localized opportunities for Huntington partner universities.Content Creation, Storytelling & Editorial-to-Social Integration: Develop skills in social-first storytelling, content production, copywriting, editing, platform adaptation and content optimization, including how advice and guidance articles can be adapted into useful, timely social plans.Creative Pitching, Collaboration & Feedback: Gain experience presenting ideas, explaining creative rationale, communicating recommendations to peers and stakeholders, and refining work through constructive feedback and collaboration.Project Management: Understand how projects move from concept to completion through planning, timelines, approvals and stakeholder coordination.Brand Standards, Compliance & Reputational Risk: Experience how content is created and reviewed within a regulated financial services environment while balancing strong creative ideas with brand standards, business objectives, risk management and reputational considerations.Measurement & Assessment: Learn how social media content is evaluated and how performance insights are used to improve future content strategies. Required SkillsStrong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present ideas clearly.Enthusiasm for social media and a thoughtful understanding of its value, influence, challenges and responsibility as a public-facing communication channel.Creativity, curiosity and willingness to contribute new ideas.Strong organizational skills, attention to detail and ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines.Comfort working independently in a remote environment and collaborating effectively with others.Openness to giving, receiving and incorporating constructive feedback. Preferred SkillsExperience creating content for personal, academic, volunteer, student organization, freelance or professional channels, including social media posts, video, photography, graphics, copywriting or other digital storytelling formats.Comfort using creative tools such as CapCut, Canva, Adobe Creative Suite, Final Cut Pro, in-app editing tools within social platforms or similar platforms to edit, design or adapt content.Interest in how social platforms work, including audience engagement, trends, platform best practices and the role social media can play in building connection, trust and action.Experience contributing to group projects, events, campaigns or creative initiatives, including presenting ideas, collaborating with peers and working toward a shared goal. QualificationsRising college junior enrolled during Summer 2027 at one of the Huntington partner schools for this program: University of Michigan, University of Minnesota, West Virginia University, University of Texas, The Ohio State University, University of Mississippi, University of Alabama or Mississippi State University.Pursuing a degree in Marketing, Communications, Journalism, Media, Advertising, Public Relations, Film, Digital Media or a related field. Application ProcessCandidates selected to advance in the interview process will be asked to complete a brief creative exercise demonstrating their understanding of social media audiences, content strategy and storytelling.

jobs.description: Employer: Camp Bear Creek Expires: 12/01/2026 Media Specialist – Summer StaffLocation: Camp Bear Creek – Eastern IowaWebsite: https://bearcreek.camp/current-job-openings/summer-camp/Dates: May 23-July 24, 2027Camp Bear Creek is a Christian summer camp in Eastern Iowa serving kids from kindergarten through 12th grade. We’re looking for passionate, fun, dedicated people who want to spend a summer making a real difference — in the lives of campers and in their own.Come work as a Media Specialist at Camp Bear Creek. We are seeking a talented individual who is ready to put their skills into practice. The Media Specialist for the summer gains a lot of experience in, well, all things media. However, you also have the chance to do a lot more than that. You'll be immersed in the summer camp environment, interacting with children and youth in a Christian setting, learning how to capture their stories and how to share the mission of the camp, the joy of the moment, and the magic of summer in something as simple as a photograph or as complex as a ten minute video.The Media Specialist is responsible for camp photography and videography. You'll be out there with the camera, whether it's a DSLR or the GoPro, capturing that kid's giant smile as they go flying down the slip 'n slide or the moment they make it to the top of the rock wall or their splash landing at the bottom of the mud slide. The Media Specialist maintains the daily summer camp blog, which parents depend on as one of their only sources of communication with their child while they're away for six days at camp. They want to know what it feels like to be at camp even when they can't be there themselves, and the best Media Specialist will be able to help them do that. The Media Specialist updates the camp social media accounts, engaging a diverse community of all ages and experiences that spans back over a 65 year history. The Media Specialist designs a weekly summary video, compiling everything that they have captured during the week and uniquely putting it all together into an 8-10 minute video that parents and campers will not only watch over and over, but they'll want to show others because it so perfectly captures what camp was like.If you think you're ready for a summer like this and to be the Media Specialist, please complete the application through the camp’s website at https://bearcreek.camp/current-job-openings/summer-camp/ You'll walk away from the summer with a bigger portfolio, college credit, and a wealth of experience. Plus, you can't discount the chance to have some fun at camp, either!

Fundraising:As needed, minimal assistance with:Building development pipelines through prospect and donor research.Donor record upkeep.Appeals/acquisitions via email and standard mail.Grant applications.Fundraising event support. LogisticsWe will consider applications for both full-time (40 hours per week) and part-time (minimum of 20 hours per week) interns for the spring term, which will start in January and conclude in May. Thus, the intern must be residing in the Washington, DC area during the internship. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment visa for internship opportunities at this time. In addition, the intern is paid a monthly stipend of $600 for part time and $1,000 for full time. Application InstructionsRSF USA welcomes current undergraduate students or recent college graduates that meet the qualifications to apply for this opportunity. We do not recommend that current postgraduate students or recent postgraduates apply. jobs.title: Production Planning Intern - Wall Plant at Haworth
jobs.description: Employer: Haworth Expires: 12/03/2026 Company OverviewAt Haworth, we're not just creating office furniture; we're shaping dynamic workspaces. As a global leader in workspace solutions, we're on a journey to redefine the future of work. Headquartered in Holland, Michigan, Haworth is a family-owned global powerhouse at the forefront of innovation and sustainable design in the workspace interiors industry. Here, you'll get hands-on with state-of-the-art resources, interact with cross-functional teams of passionate innovators, and experience a blend of global reach and family-owned feel. Whether you're developing new manufacturing processes, implementing smart factory solutions, or designing tomorrow's workspace solutions, you'll be empowered to make a lasting impact.We are currently looking for paid Production Planning Intern to join our team in Holland, MI. This position will be working onsite at the Haworth Corporate Headquarters.Job OverviewGet ready for an adventurous summer as a Haworth intern! You'll join a cohort of around 50 other dynamic interns for a 12-week program packed with meaningful projects and weekly learning opportunities. You'll attend NeoCon, the largest commercial design event in the world, where you will get an insider's look at all the latest industry trends and innovations. Sharpen your skills with interactive workshops on networking, public speaking, and using AI tools in a business environment. Connect with mentors and see all areas of the office and manufacturing processes. Then unwind at intern-only social events where you can meet people from all corners of the business. By the end of the summer, you'll leave with real skills, an expanded professional network, and memories to last a lifetime. This is your chance to take your career to new heights!As a Production Planning intern, you will have the opportunity to assist with a variety of exciting projects including: analyzing production and planning data to better understand schedule performance, capacity constraints, and production challenges while exploring how AI tools can help identify solutions and develop recommendations for improvement.Required QualificationsPart-time or full-time college enrollment, working towards a bachelor's degree in Supply Chain Management, Manufacturing Management, Business Management or similar with at least a junior level status by Fall of 2027.Ability to work On-site in Holland, MI from May 2027 to August 2027.Applicants must possess an unrestricted right to work in the US to be eligible for the position.Familiarity with CoPilot or similar AI tools and an interest in using AI to support data analysis, problem-solving, and process improvement.Ability to independently use Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace applications for everyday business activities, including creating documents and presentations, working with spreadsheets, managing email and calendars, and collaborating through shared files and virtual meeting toolPreferred QualificationsOverall GPA of 2.95 or higher.Prior Haworth experience.Previous Employment experience.Extra-curricular activity experience such as athletics, clubs, volunteer work, etc.Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel, with the ability to analyze complex data, create PivotTables, use macros, and develop reports.Familiarity with SAP or similar ERP systems used for production planning, inventory, or materials management.Ideally, you have also demonstrated the following:Ability to work with minimal supervision.Desire to learn, question, and research solutions to problems.Organized with the ability to manage deadlines.Good verbal and written communication skills.

With more than 1 billion loyal users globally, we believe TikTok is an ideal platform to deliver a brand new and better e-commerce experience to our users. Candidates may apply to a maximum of two positions across Our Company and its affiliates globally. Applications will be considered in the order they are submitted. Internship experience in e-commerce or having a solid understanding of the industry landscape is a plusFamiliar with TikTok and other content platforms; experience in content-based eCommerce (brand and/or platform-side) is highly preferred.Strong network and connections with brands and/or retailers is a plus.Passion for TikTok and eCommerce, eager to exceed challenging goals while building something truly unique to the market.CompensationThe hourly rate range for this position in Los Angeles is $23.75 - $23.75.Benefits may vary depending on the nature of employment and the country work location. Interns have day one access to health insurance, life insurance, wellbeing benefits and more. Interns also receive 10 paid holidays per year and paid sick time (56 hours if hired in first half of year, 40 if hired in second half of year). Interns who are not working 100% remote may also be eligible for housing allowance.The Company reserves the right to modify or change these benefits programs at any time, with or without notice.For Los Angeles County (unincorporated) CandidatesQualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment in accordance with all federal, state, and local laws including the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers and the California Fair Chance Act. Our company believes that criminal history may have a direct, adverse and negative relationship on the following job duties, potentially resulting in the withdrawal of the conditional offer of employment:Interacting and occasionally having unsupervised contact with internal/external clients and/or colleagues;Appropriately handling and managing confidential information including proprietary and trade secret information and access to information technology systems; andExercising sound judgment.About TikTokTikTok is the leading destination for short-form mobile video. At TikTok, our mission is to inspire creativity and bring joy. TikTok's global headquarters are in Los Angeles and Singapore, and we also have offices in New York City, London, Dublin, Paris, Berlin, Dubai, Jakarta, Seoul, and Tokyo.Why Join UsInspiring creativity is at the core of TikTok's mission. Our innovative product is built to help people authentically express themselves, discover and connect – and our global, diverse teams make that possible. Together, we create value for our communities, inspire creativity and bring joy - a mission we work towards every day.We strive to do great things with great people. We lead with curiosity, humility, and a desire to make impact in a rapidly growing tech company. Every challenge is an opportunity to learn and innovate as one team. We're resilient and embrace challenges as they come. By constantly iterating and fostering an "Always Day 1" mindset, we achieve meaningful breakthroughs for ourselves, our company, and our users. When we create and grow together, the possibilities are limitless. Join us.Diversity & InclusionTikTok is committed to creating an inclusive space where employees are valued for their skills, experiences, and unique perspectives. jobs.description: Employer: TikTok Inc. Expires: 12/04/2026 AI Safety Evaluation & Governance Product Manager Intern (TikTok-Platform Responsibility-Feed Safety) - 2027 SummerLocation: San JoseEmployment Type: InternJob Code: A195925 ResponsibilitiesAbout the Team The Feed Safety-Model & Data Intelligence team within TikTok Platform Responsibility ensures that AI models meet the highest bar before they make content safety decisions affecting billions of users. Our work spans three layers: - Standards & Governance — We define and iterate the safety standards that AI systems must follow, translating complex policy intent into structured, machine-interpretable frameworks. This requires deep governance thinking: navigating trade-offs between safety, fairness, user experience, and enforcement consistency. - AI/ML Solution Design — We partner closely with algorithm teams to improve model accuracy and stability across safety scenarios, tackling challenges unique to this domain — adversarial content, imbalanced distributions, and deep contextual understanding. We evaluate, select, and help shape the right AI approaches (LLMs, prompting strategies, agentic workflows, etc.) for each problem. - Rigorous Evaluation — We design statistically grounded evaluation frameworks, build high-quality ground truth datasets, and ensure our assessments are valid, reproducible, and actionable — so the platform can confidently ship AI-powered safety systems at scale. Our work sits at the intersection of AI/ML product development, trust & safety policy, and data-driven quality assurance — ensuring that AI systems can be reliably deployed for high-precision content review and risk governance at scale. Our internship program offers students hands-on experience, industry exposure, and opportunities to apply their knowledge to real-world challenges while building a strong foundation for personal and professional growth.
